notes.subject: plate
notes.text: Newest plates are white with black characters, four letters then three digits, under a blue top band with the country name, flag and Mercosur logo.

notes.subject: plate
notes.text: Plates from 2000 to 2019 are white with red characters, three letters then three digits, with flag top-left, name top-centre and a national emblem top-right.

notes.subject: plate
notes.text: Motorcycle plates reverse the order, with the digits first and the letters after.

notes.subject: plate
notes.text: Diplomatic plates are black with white characters, using letters like CD, CC or MOE followed by six digits.

notes.subject: plate
notes.text: Pre-2000 plates outside the capital were mostly white with red characters, starting with a letter for the department; in the capital they were blue with white numbers.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Warning signs are yellow diamonds, as across most of the Americas.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Road sign standards are based on North American and Latin American manuals, so many designs resemble those of the US, Mexico, Colombia and Chile.

notes.subject: language
notes.text: Two official languages, one of them indigenous and spoken by over 90% of people, so local-language words appear next to the colonial-era one.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Web domains end in .py and the phone code is +595.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: The east has grassy plains and wooded hills, with plenty of rainfall.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: The west is low, marshy plains turning semi-arid in the far west, with much less rain than the east.
